speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Education how will the period of home-based learning and school closures affect students applying to Secondary schools under the Direct School Admission programme.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But there will need to be some adjustments in how schools evaluate the students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Since 2018, we have been making some significant changes to the DSA process and there are three.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, we moved DSA away from being an evaluation of general academic abilities, and instead, focused on specific talents and aptitudes of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, with that shift, we encouraged more schools to participate with their respective niche talent development programmes, and as a result, we expanded the number of DSA places on offer.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These changes are part of our continuing effort to recognise students’ abilities for admission to Secondary schools, beyond using PSLE exam results.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In selecting students for DSA, schools will continue to uphold the principles of transparency, objectivity, inclusiveness and student-centricity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, the evaluation methods will have to change as we need to observe safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will not be able to depend on traditional selection methods like trials and auditions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Instead, our schools will implement the following measures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, schools will conduct interviews through video-conferencing tools, which our students, teachers are now all very familiar with.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These sessions will take place from early July to middle of September, so a couple of months away.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They will be scheduled and spaced out to avoid inter-mingling of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Schools may also conduct simple e-auditions in a similar way, for arts categories such as singing, dancing or drama.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, without selection trials and with the suspension of National School Games, Secondary schools will need to give more recognition to the student’s talent, potential, passion and character through their school track record, and information provided in the students’ online applications.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Schools will look out for the student’s demonstrated dedication to a sport and their training attitude, even without a placement in the National School Games.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is not entirely new, but if the circumstances this year force schools to re-evaluate their definition of a good sportsperson, I think it is not a bad outcome at all.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Each school will have to decide how it wants to evaluate a student, and apply it consistently and fairly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, our Primary schools will step up efforts to encourage students with ability and potential, especially those from less advantaged family backgrounds, to apply through DSA to suitable schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will ensure that students from less advantaged backgrounds have equitable opportunities to access DSA.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: COVID-19 has taken away regular classes, and also our tried and tested methods of grading and DSA selection.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But instead of stalling our education reforms, it has underscored their importance and provided impetus for us to journey on.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, we recognised the importance of digital literacy – we always did – but acceptance of online learning tools and capabilities across schools were uneven, and we therefore needed a fairly lengthy phase-in period that I announced in Parliament during the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But now having forced everyone into home-based learning, that has helped us overcome that problem almost overnight.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We always wanted to emphasise more on Character and Citizenship Education and especially moral education, and COVID-19 has provided us with many important teaching moments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Similarly, we have progressively been reducing the over-emphasis on examinations and grades in our current system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Now, COVID-19 is forcing us to adopt more alternate evaluation tools and make greater efforts to exercise judgement on the potential and character of a child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, education reforms will therefore continue and so will the DSA exercise, and all the more so this year.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a school sportsman who spent more time on the field than in the classroom, I have had been a huge fan of DSA.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad to know that DSA will continue for this year.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do understand that there will be challenges for different types of students applying under DSA.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, it might be easier to arrange for e-auditions and e-interviews for those using the arts or drama.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Minister mentioned something about the students who are participating in sports in lieu of the national sports games or time trials.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am just wondering, Minister, for many of these individual sportsman, especially, the timings of that particular sports would determine sometimes whether or not they are able to qualify for the programme in certain schools.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Minister or the Ministry be able to clarify how will the schools be more transparent, perhaps, ensuring that there are some common guidelines or common practices across all the schools with regard to say accepting students who are swimmers, athletes or tennis players in the absence of objective qualifying times, which would have been the case if there had been national sports games or even national time trials.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First, for artistic talent, I do not think the community will feel it is easy to go with e-auditions; it is a challenge.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you watch an e-audition, you can judge and evaluate how hard have this child been training, how much effort they have put in, how passionate and dedicated they are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are also no time trials for arts but you just have to make that judgement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It may have to well apply to sports this year, there being no national games; there is no timing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But this is one of our habits as an education system and as a society as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We always like to boil everything down to one number and we compare the number, whose number is bigger and smaller and, therefore, you enter.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is in a way how life is.
